subject: Acme feature parity - function calling / streaming follow-up
messages:
From: Jamie Kim <jamie.kim@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Brown <alex.brown@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-25T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Acme - follow-up & evaluation criteria

Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning — that was really helpful. As discussed, we want to run a short competitive evaluation focused on three areas:

- Function/tool calling (schema validation, latency, reliability)
- Structured outputs (JSON/YAML enforcement, hallucination rates)
- Streaming & partial-response behavior (token latency, chunk size, reconnects)

High-level asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood provide a short feature-parity matrix compared to the hyperscalers (Google/Anthropic/AWS endpoints) for those items?
2) Can we get a sandbox/demo instance or credentials to run the tests?
3) Any suggested telemetry/metrics we should capture (e.g., p50/p95 per-token latency, returned tokens per second, schema validation failures)?

Goal: one-week quick evaluation, then a tech deep-dive if results look promising. Alex from procurement is cc'd to loop in contracting later.

Thanks,

Jamie Kim
Head of AI Platforms
Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Kim <jamie.kim@acme.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-25T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme - follow-up & evaluation criteria

Jamie — great to connect. Summary and proposed next steps below. Attaching a short matrix (redwood_vs_hyperscaler_matrix.xlsx) that maps feature parity and our recommended test cases.

Summary of what we heard:
- Priority tests: function calling reliability + schema enforcement, structured JSON outputs for billing/line-item extraction, and end-to-end streaming behavior for real-time UI.
- Evaluation constraints: 1-week sandbox, representative prompt set, and automated checks for schema validation + latency.

Proposed next steps:
1) We will provide a sandbox API key and a small test harness (postman collection + basic curl examples).
2) Mateo will run a short demo of function calling and streaming behavior with your prompt set — can do Tue 6/30 or Wed 7/1 for a 45-min tech session.
3) We'll deliver the matrix (attached) and a recommended telemetry plan (p50/p95 token latency, schema-failure-rate, token-cost-per-call).

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_matrix.xlsx

Telemetry we suggest capturing:
- p50/p95 per-token latency (with streaming enabled)
- end-to-end time to first token
- schema validation pass/fail and example mismatches
- token usage and cost estimates per test case

If that timeline works, I'll send sandbox creds and the prompt set template.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Jamie Kim <jamie.kim@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Brown <alex.brown@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-26T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme - follow-up & evaluation criteria

Thanks Marissa. Tue 6/30 10:00am PT works for the tech session — please calendar with Mateo.

A couple of clarifications from our side before the sandbox:
- For function calling: we'll validate both sync (single-shot) and async (long-running) calls. Will Redwood support callback/webhook patterns for async responses?
- For structured outputs: we'll feed in an existing invoice extraction prompt set (about 250 prompts). Can you confirm an output size cap and recommended batch size?

Also looping Alex so procurement can confirm the sandbox terms. Can you include any SOC2 or data residency notes up front?

Jamie

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Kim <jamie.kim@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-27T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme - follow-up & evaluation criteria — tech notes and tests

Jamie — quick technical note ahead of Tue's session. Short answers first:
- Async callbacks: yes, we support webhook-style async delivery for long-running function-call workflows. We also expose streaming-first-chunk callbacks for immediate UI updates.
- Output size cap: default response token cap is 8,192 tokens per response in sandbox; we can expand for evaluation if needed. Recommended batch size for structured-extraction: 8-16 concurrent requests per worker depending on sequence length.

Planned tests we'll run together:
1) Function calling (sync): 100 samples, measure schema pass-rate and latency (p50/p95).
2) Function calling (async): 50 long-running samples with webhook retries and idempotency checks.
3) Structured extraction: run 250 invoice prompts in batches of 10; capture JSON schema validation failures and token cost.
4) Streaming: exercise 4 different chunk sizes and measure time-to-first-token and steady-state tokens/sec.

Attachments included for reference: streaming-demo.mp4 (short recording of streaming behavior), eval-results.json (example output schema + a few failure cases).

Implementation notes:
- We recommend validating JSON with our lightweight JSON schema checker in the client (we'll provide it in the repo).
- For cost comparison vs hyperscalers, use per-token billed units and normalized tokenization (we included a normalization row in the attached matrix).

I'll bring logs and a short demo to the call. Looking forward — Mateo

Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai

From: Jamie Kim <jamie.kim@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Brown <alex.brown@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme - follow-up & evaluation criteria — tech notes and tests

Perfect — thanks, Mateo and Marissa. We've scheduled Tue 6/30 10:00am PT and will send our prompt set and a sample schema tonight. A couple of final logistics items:

- Sandbox creds: Alex — can you confirm the account/email we should whitelist? We plan to use a small set of internal test hosts.
- SOC2/docs: If you can share a short SOC2 & data residency note ahead of the session, procurement will be happier.
- Success criteria for us: schema pass-rate >= 95% for structured extraction and streaming time-to-first-token < 350ms p95.

We'll run the first day of tests against Redwood and then run the same harness against the hyperscaler endpoints for a parity comparison. If Redwood meets the success criteria and cost is reasonable, we'll ask for a short pilot contract.

Thanks again — looking forward to the demo.

Jamie Kim
Head of AI Platforms | Acme Corp
